script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. Monday — here is your MEME recap. The portfolio closed two point four six percent down on the session. Two names drove the damage. Both deserve your full attention.

Sandisk plunged eleven point zero two percent on Monday after Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT rocketed in its Shanghai IPO, rattling the entire memory sector and raising the immediate question of how deep the competitive damage runs.

Crude oil tumbled sharply on the session as reports of progress toward a United States-Iran peace framework eased geopolitical risk premiums, pulling energy prices down and weighing on sentiment across rate-sensitive growth names. The Nasdaq moved lower as semiconductor losses dominated the tape, with memory and optical names bearing the heaviest pressure.

The dominant story of Monday's session belongs to Sandisk. The stock fell eleven point zero two percent after Chinese rival CXMT completed a high-profile IPO on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, sending shares of memory-focused names broadly lower. Micron and SK Hynix also dropped on the news. The concern is structural: CXMT's market debut signals accelerating Chinese domestic memory capacity, which carries direct pricing pressure implications for NAND and broader memory markets where Sandisk competes. Compounding the selloff, a separate report noted that a Chinese state-backed company announced mass production of domestic chip-making equipment, adding a second layer of supply-chain anxiety to an already pressured sector. This position represents five percent of the portfolio, and Monday's move was the second-largest single-day loss across all nine primary holdings.

Turning to Applied Optoelectronics, the largest position in the portfolio at seven point four three percent of holdings — it fell two point three three percent on Monday. The stock has been sensitive to broader optical and data-center infrastructure sentiment, and Monday's weakness in semiconductor names created headwinds across the space. Watch for any commentary following Bloom Energy's earnings report Tuesday that addresses data-center power demand, which has been a driver of optical interconnect volume.

Redwire Corporation rose one point six one percent on Monday, making it one of the session's cleaner performers in the portfolio. No specific company news drove the move, but the industrials and space infrastructure segment showed relative resilience. Lumentum Holdings was the opposite story — the stock collapsed fourteen point six zero percent on Monday, the single largest decline across all nine primary holdings. At five point five zero percent of the portfolio, that is a material hit. No direct company-specific catalyst was immediately attributed to the move, but the broader optical and photonics sector faced significant selling pressure, and any read-through from datacom demand softness would be a key concern. Watch closely for analyst commentary in the coming sessions.

AST SpaceMobile gained three point seven two percent on Monday, the strongest performer in the portfolio. The company announced it will host its second quarter twenty-twenty-six business update call on August tenth at five p.m. Eastern Time, giving investors a clear near-term catalyst. Separately, a report highlighted Amazon's proposed five thousand one hundred five-satellite direct-to-phone constellation, which intensifies the competitive backdrop even as AST SpaceMobile remains the most advanced operator in the space-based cellular broadband category.

Nebius Group was essentially flat, closing up just zero point zero six percent. An analyst piece cited the company's relationship with Nvidia as a structural advantage, projecting potential revenue multiplication over three years. The neocloud infrastructure thesis remains intact here. Bloom Energy added one point seven eight percent ahead of its second quarter earnings report due Tuesday, July twenty-eighth. Analysts have noted the bar was raised following record first quarter results, and the Oracle and Brookfield partnership deals will be closely scrutinized for revenue contribution. TeraWulf fell two point six zero percent. Wall Street raised price targets above thirty dollars on the name, yet the stock declined — a divergence worth monitoring as the market signals it wants execution evidence before rewarding the AI infrastructure pivot. Lumentum's move was covered above. IREN Limited slipped two point one zero percent, in line with broader pressure on bitcoin mining and AI infrastructure names. No specific news drove the move.

Three specific items demand attention in the next forty-eight hours. First, Bloom Energy reports second quarter earnings on Tuesday, July twenty-eighth — this is a direct catalyst for a nearly six percent portfolio position, and guidance on data-center power contracts will set the tone. Second, AST SpaceMobile's August tenth business update call is now confirmed — investors should begin framing expectations around satellite deployment progress and commercial partnership updates. Third, any follow-on analyst notes addressing the CXMT IPO impact on NAND pricing will be critical for assessing whether Monday's Sandisk decline reflects a one-session reaction or the beginning of a sustained repricing of the memory sector.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Keep Bloom Energy's earnings report at the top of your watch list — the read-through on AI power demand could move more than one name in this portfolio.
